description: Committed UI-protocol manifest (feature 044). Single source for the server->client WS frame vocabulary, the ui_event action vocabulary, and the component vocabulary. Backend, Windows, and Android test suites all assert against this file; adding a frame type, action, or component type REQUIRES editing it in the same PR (guards fail otherwise). See specs/044-native-client-parity/contracts/ui-protocol.md.

ordinary_settings_forms.options: String choices or objects with a string value and readable label. Labels are displayed, values submitted, and saved choices absent from refreshed catalogs remain recoverable.
ordinary_settings_forms.defaults: Untouched select, boolean and checklist controls display and submit their saved defaults; conditional fields use the same resolved form state.
ordinary_settings_forms.actions: Untyped label/action/payload descriptors are metadata, not renderable components. Adaptation preserves routing and labels, while host interactivity and action budgets still apply. Missing routing is explicitly unavailable.

native_result.request_generation: Optional canonical lowercase UUID4 copied from the initiating request only for its registry-owned surface and current socket. The candidate server echoes every valid ordinary request generation.
native_result.ownership: A supplied payload surface can only match the action handler's registry-owned surface; it cannot redirect a response to another form.
native_result.close: An ordinary accepted action may echo its exact canonical request_generation on an empty surface_key modal replace close, with empty title/components, admin_only false and no selection. The server closes only the current socket/owner/generation; queued same-surface or different-surface navigation retires the previous request. Mandatory account setup transitions retain their authoritative uncorrelated close.
native_result.client: Require the exact pending generation whenever an echo is present. Legacy uncorrelated ordinary results may settle only the current surface/socket's single pending operation.
